s: a microscopic, unrestored hideaway on a picturesque Old Town square
w: True to its name -- the "Small Café" -- this is one of Vienna's tiniest coffeehouses, its unrestored facade and pint-sized interior on Franziskanerplatz barely hinting at how long locals have loved it. Designed by architect Hermann Czech, it runs on laidback, slightly countercultural charm rather than gilt and marble, with beer and a sausage as much a fixture as the coffee.
_facts: Located at Franziskanerplatz 3, 1010 Wien, Innere Stadt
One of Vienna's smallest coffeehouses, with limited interior seating
Interior designed by Austrian architect Hermann Czech
Known for an unrestored, lived-in aesthetic on a picturesque small square

s: a generational café where grandmothers and grandfathers bake and serve
w: A café built on a simple, moving idea: retired Viennese grandmothers and grandfathers, in bright aprons, bake the cakes and run the floor, earning extra income and staying connected rather than isolated. Buchteln with vanilla sauce arrive in a room styled like an actual grandparents' living room -- sofas, mismatched china, warmth over polish -- in the creative Freihausviertel near the Naschmarkt.
_facts: Located at Schleifmühlgasse 16, 1040 Wien, Freihausviertel, Wieden
"Generational café" concept: retired grandmothers and grandfathers bake and serve
Set up partly to address old-age poverty and loneliness among Vienna's elderly
Has a second location at Johannesgasse 4a in the 1st district

s: an artsy coffeehouse with 1960s decor and a basement bowling alley
w: A coffeehouse near St Stephen's Cathedral that skips the gilt-and-marble template for original 1960s retro decor, rotating art on the walls, and -- down a staircase -- a small basement bowling alley doubling as an informal art lounge. A long-standing gathering point for Vienna's artists and creatives rather than a period piece.
_facts: Located at Brandstätte 9, 1010 Wien, Innere Stadt, near St Stephen's Cathedral
Has a basement bowling alley that doubles as an art/exhibition space
Long-running gathering spot for artists and creatives

s: a 1910 Jugendstil coffeehouse under monument protection, off the main tourist run
w: Founded in 1910 by the Dobner coffeehouse family, Café Goldegg mixes classic Viennese coffeehouse form with Jugendstil-era detail -- inlaid wood panelling, black-and-white marble tables, dark green banquettes, brass chandeliers. A careful 1988-89 restoration put it under monument protection; today it runs on local regulars rather than the tour-group circuit.
_facts: Founded in 1910 by the Dobner family
Interior combines traditional coffeehouse form with Jugendstil (Art Nouveau) design elements
Restored 1988-89 with support from the Vienna Old Town Preservation Fund; under monument protection
